external_entities.name: Shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: Card Processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: Storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that provides the storefront and accepts payment-status webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: Order Service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders and writes receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The worker receives the database password from an environment variable.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: Receipt Archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts that record the order written and that the order service wrote it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: A shopper browses the storefront and places orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.notes: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.
data_flows.data_description: orders and shopper account sign-in data

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: payment settlement status for an order

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud Run
trust_boundaries.description: The Cloud Run hosting zone in which the storefront API runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run

trust_boundaries.name: Core Network
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's core network containing the order service.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because it is the HTTP-facing storefront API and receives a POST webhook.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the storefront API as the internet-exposed storefront and says the card processor POSTs a webhook to it.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database contains confidential data because it stores shopper addresses and card-last-four values alongside orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive contains confidential data because it stores payment-related order receipts.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the store as a receipt archive for completed orders.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive contains financial data because it stores receipts for completed orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order gets a receipt written to the archive.
